header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Dana Morales (Redwood AE); Elliot Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Kapoor (Redwood Product); Maya Singh (Verdant, Head of ML); Ravi Patel (Verdant, Eng Manager); Tom Alvarez (Verdant, Security); Laura Kim (Verdant, Product)
summary: Demo focused on response contracts (JSON mode), execution sandbox for tool/function calling, guardrails and how Console + Optimize recommendations reduce token costs. Customer wants clarity on data residency, KMS, and a 2-week pilot to validate latency & output fidelity.
transcript:
00:00 Dana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Dana from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll run a quick 30 minute ish demo, then leave time for Q&A — Elliot will show the sandbox.
00:10 Maya: Thanks Dana, excited. We're particularly interested in how you can guarantee structured outputs for downstream pipelines — we're using a typed schema in our ingestion.
00:25 Elliot: Great, that's what JSON mode is for — we can enforce contracts, type-check, and have automatic fallbacks if the model returns mal-formed json. I'll pull up the Console.
00:40 Ravi: Quick one — are these schemas enforced at runtime or post-hoc? We have a strict validator before inserting to the data lake.
00:55 Elliot: They run at runtime in the runtime layer. We validate the produced payload against the schema and if mismatch, you can configure a fallback like re-ask, call a sanitizer tool, or route to a lower-latency shim.
01:20 Tom: Security question — any of this payloads persist in hosted mode? What's the retention and are they encrypted with our KMS?
01:32 Dana: Short answer: hosted keeps minimal logs by default — you can opt into no-retention for PII. For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and VPC. We'll send the SOC2 packet after.
01:50 Elliot: Ok moving to the sandbox — I'm provisioning a session where Verdant devs can run requests against an aurora model variant we prepped. Note: model variant is quantized to reduce cost; Console shows perf profile.
02:10 Speaker 1: (crosstalk) does that change tokenization?
02:16 Elliot: It can change per-token latency slightly, but Optimize gives quantization suggestions per workload.
02:35 Elliot: I'm switching to the JSON mode demo — schema is declared in the Console as an OpenAPI-like contract, but more strictly typed for responses. Here's a sample: {"type": "object", "properties": { "customer_id": { "type": "string" }, "recommendations": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object" } } } } — keep in mind transcription might garble some punctuation.
03:15 Laura: If the model halluc's an extra field, will the ingest fail?
03:22 Elliot: You can set 'strict' or 'permissive' mode. In strict, it fails and triggers the fallback flow. In permissive it strips unknown fields, which is useful for backwards compat.
03:50 Maya: Can you demonstrate a tool call — we want the LLM to call our enrichment service and then return a merged JSON.
04:05 Elliot: Yep — I'll wire a toy 'enrichProfile' tool into the sandbox. Watch this: request -> model decides to call enrichProfile(tool args) -> runtime invokes the tool securely in the sandbox -> tool returns structured data -> model composes final JSON.
04:40 Elliot: (typing) Sending a prompt: 'Given profile X, call enrichProfile then return final customer_payload matching schema v2.'
05:05 System: Tool enrichProfile invoked with args {"email": "m.singh@verdant.io"} (note: email redacted in recording).
05:30 Ravi: How are credentials handled for calling customer tools? We don't want Redwood to store secrets.
05:40 Elliot: In Private/Dedicated you store credentials in your vault and we forward them from your VPC — Redwood does not persist them. For hosted we support ephemeral creds and token passthroughs. We'll document exact flows in the security pack.
06:10 Maya: Also latency matters. If the tool call takes 800ms, will the overall prompt time blow up?
06:25 Elliot: The runtime exposes per-step latency SLOs; Console will show per-tool timing and you can set timeouts and fallback policies. Also Optimize may recommend caching prefixes for common enrich calls.
07:00 Dana: Quick pause — shout if I'm going too fast.
07:05 Maya: No, good.
07:18 Elliot: Demo result: model returned a perfectly shaped JSON, matched schema v2, and Console flagged zero errors. Now I'll simulate a failing tool: tool returns malformed payload and show fallback.
07:45 System: Tool enrichProfile returned malformed field 'dob': 'Febt 31 1990'
07:53 Elliot: The runtime validated, mismatch detected, we triggered the 'sanitize' tool which ran a second pass and corrected the date to '1990-02-28' and model re-composed. You can chain these sanitizers.
08:28 Ravi: Nice. For our pipelines we need deterministic outputs — can you guarantee stability across model versions?
08:40 Elliot: Not absolute guarantee, but Console's rollout supports canary and A/B test, and Optimize gives you quant profiles and a 'semantic drift' monitor. If quality drops, you can auto-fallback to previous model.
09:05 Laura: How do prompts get versioned? We have many templates.
09:12 Priya: We store prompt sets as named artifacts in the Console with version metadata; evals can run against them to detect regressions.
09:25 Maya: Ok for the pilot — success criteria: 95% schema-validated outputs over 10k calls and average 350ms p50 latency. We want a dashboard that tracks both fidelity and token cost.
09:40 Dana: That fits a standard pilot. We'll schedule a 2-week sandbox with 10k sample requests. We'll send a proposed SOW.
10:00 Tom: Security follow-up — we need to confirm data residency. Our EU customers require data to remain in eu-west-1.
10:10 Dana: We can pin region routing for requests; for Private/Dedicated you can run in your VPC in eu-west-1. We'll capture region info in the SOW.
10:28 Ravi: On cost — quantization sounds great. Can we get an estimate for tokens saved if we batch versus single-shot?
10:38 Priya: Optimize has a cost simulator — you can input request volume & avg length and it'll recommend batching windows, KV cache TTLs, and quant settings. We'll include a sample run for Verdant's profile.
11:05 Elliot: Switching to live Console: here's the model catalog — aurora-small-8q is the variant we've prepared. See per-token latency, per-token cost, and suggested batch size 16 for your throughput.
11:35 Elliot: I'm enabling the 'execution sandbox' now — you'll get a join link. This sandbox runs in a locked environment with logging disabled by default and sanitized output.
12:00 System: (link shared) https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/VDNT-2027-0041 (redacted in transcript)
12:20 Maya: Who from our side should get access? Ravi and two engineers.
12:30 Dana: We'll invite Ravi, Laura, and your ML engineer, Maya — Elliot will provision.
12:40 Elliot: Provisioning now — you should get invites within 30 minutes. The sandbox includes sample tools: enrichProfile, lookupPricing, and a sanitizer chain.
13:05 Laura: If we want to run our own enrichment service behind our firewall, can the sandbox call it?
13:15 Elliot: Yes — for private setups we can configure outbound rules to your IP ranges or set up a VPC peering. For hosted, we recommend using a secure connector with ephemeral credentials.
13:40 Tom: On compliance, we also need audit logs for who invoked what. Are logs immutable and exportable to our SIEM?
13:55 Dana: Yes — audit logs are exportable to S3 or to your SIEM via forwarders; for Private we support HSM-backed signing and longer retention. We'll include the retention table in the security pack.
14:20 Ravi: About function calling safety — can we define an allowlist of tools per model/prompt? We don't want the model to call arbitrary tools unexpectedly.
14:31 Elliot: Absolutely. The runtime has tool-level RBAC and allowlist per route. You can also set rate limits per tool and per-API key.
15:00 Maya: Let's see a failure mode where model tries an unauthorized tool.
15:10 Elliot: (runs demo) Model attempted 'destroy_customer' (toy name) — runtime blocked it and returned a structured error code: {"error": "unauthorized_tool_call", "tool": "destroy_customer", "allowed_tools": ["enrichProfile", "lookupPricing"]}. Console logged the event and we can trigger an alert.
15:45 Ravi: Great. For pilot instrumentation, we need token-level cost breakdown per route.
15:55 Elliot: Console provides token-level breakdowns, and Optimize can run a monthly batch analysis to recommend quantization and batching changes.
16:20 Laura: Are there any known edge cases with streaming responses + JSON mode? We stream tokens but need to ensure we don't end up with partial JSON to downstream services.
16:35 Elliot: Good call — we support chunked streaming but also 'atomic output' mode which waits to validate full JSON before emitting to the client. That adds minimal latency but ensures deterministic outputs.
17:00 Tom: For SSO, we use Okta. How does user sync work?
17:10 Dana: We support SAML/Okta SSO and SCIM provisioning. We can sync groups and map them to Console roles for RBAC.
17:30 Maya: Ok this looks promising. A couple of clarifying items on the SOW: pilot cost, who pays for Dedicated if we need it, and SLAs during pilot.
17:45 Dana: We'll propose a trial credit model for the sandbox; Dedicated would be a separate contract. Pilot SLA is our standard 99% for hosted; Dedicated has higher SLA options in the SOW.
18:05 Priya: One more product note — Optimize will ingest your sample traffic and recommend three quantization profiles; we can baseline quality on your prompt set.
18:25 Ravi: Can the sandbox lock model versions so our tests are repeatable?
18:33 Elliot: Yes — we'll pin model SHA/version for the sandbox and you'll be able to snapshot the runtime config.
18:50 Maya: Let's talk about the 2-week cadence: Day 0 - onboarding & seed data; days 1-3 - initial runs; days 4-10 - load & regressions; day 11-13 - evaluation; day 14 - wrap & decision.
19:10 Dana: Sounds good, we'll mirror that in the SOW.
19:25 System: (15 minute demo excerpt ends — Q&A continues)
19:40 Speaker 2: (garbled) sorry missed last part, can you repeat the sandbox link?
19:48 Dana: Link is shared in chat and Elliot will re-send.
20:05 Elliot: Re-sending sandbox invite now.
20:20 Tom: One more on encryption — at-rest and in-transit ok but we need to enforce BYOK for keys.
20:30 Dana: We support BYOK via customer KMS for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports dedicated key handles with restricted export. We'll include specifics.
20:55 Ravi: For the pilot we'll likely start with hosted sandbox, then evaluate Dedicated if throughput or residency demands it.
21:10 Dana: Makes sense, low friction to start hosted.
21:30 Maya: Are there any performance numbers you can share for similar customers?
21:40 Elliot: For e-comm recommendation workloads we've seen p50 ~200-400ms with quantized variants and batching; token cost reductions of 30-60% vs baseline. We'll include anonymized benchmarks.
22:05 Laura: Ok — next steps again?
22:12 Dana: We'll send SOW, provision sandbox, include SOC2/security pack, and run an Optimize simulation for your workload. Expect invites + docs within 24 hours.
22:30 Maya: Perfect. Thanks team.
22:40 Dana: Thanks everyone — Elliot will follow up to provision and Tom we'll loop on KMS questions.
22:50 System: Meeting ended.
47:30 (file end - transcript truncated to conserve recording size; full console logs available in the sandbox link)
